description: Make Quip pairing work via a tappable quip://pair share link (AirDrop/Messages/Mail) and obtainable remotely, without depending on the native iOS Camera. Swift/Xcode; quality gate = xcodebuild build + XCTest (no lint/tsc/pytest in this repo).

userStories.title: Unit-test the PairingPayload encode/decode contract
userStories.description: As a developer, I want PairingPayload round-trip + parse coverage so the shared pairing-link format cannot silently regress.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Shared/Tests/PairingPayloadTests.swift using XCTest with @testable import Quip, wired into the QuipiOSTests target
Test: PairingPayload(url:pin:).encodedURL() then PairingPayload.decode(...) preserves url and pin exactly (round-trip)
Test: a quip://pair?url=<base64-no-pad>&pin=<digits> string decodes to the original ws/wss URL (base64 re-padding works)
Test: malformed input (wrong scheme, missing url, missing or empty pin, non-base64) returns nil
Test: a plain ws:// or wss:// non-quip string decodes to nil so callers fall back to the raw-URL path (matches current contract)
xcodebuild test -project QuipiOS/QuipiOS.xcodeproj -scheme QuipiOS -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -only-testing:QuipiOSTests/PairingPayloadTests passes
userStories.notes: Shared/Tests/PairingPayloadTests.swift (13 tests). xcodegen regen wired it into QuipiOSTests; build-for-testing + test-without-building on booted iPhone 17 Pro (id=CFCE8360) both green — 13/13 pass. Headless test runs fine when the sim is already booted (use test-without-building).

userStories.title: Pair by tapping a quip://pair link (iOS onOpenURL)
userStories.description: As a remote user, I want to tap a shared quip://pair link and have the phone pair automatically, so I never need the on-screen QR or the native Camera.
acceptanceCriteria: Extract the QRScannerView sheet's decode-and-pair block (QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift around line 1637) into one helper applyPairingPayload(_ payload: PairingPayload) that calls manager.addPaired + KeychainBackendPINs.write + manager.setActive + connect
onOpenURL (QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift around line 310) handles url.host == "pair": decode via PairingPayload.decode(url.absoluteString), call applyPairingPayload, and return BEFORE the window/perms branch
The in-app QR scanner sheet calls the SAME helper (no duplicated pairing logic)
Existing quip://window/<id>, quip://perms, and .quippack deep links still work unchanged
xcodebuild build -project QuipiOS/QuipiOS.xcodeproj -scheme QuipiOS -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' succeeds

userStories.title: Pairing URL reflects the active network mode
userStories.description: As a remote user, I want the pairing link to embed a URL reachable from where I am, so Tailscale mode uses the ts.net/100.x URL instead of a useless .local address.
acceptanceCriteria: pairingURL() in QuipMac/Views/SettingsView.swift branches on networkMode: .tailscale -> TailscaleService.webSocketURL (ts.net / 100.x), .cloudflareTunnel -> tunnel.webSocketURL, .localOnly -> LAN/.local
SecurityTab gets TailscaleService and networkMode injected so the branch can read them
In .tailscale mode the embedded URL is the ts.net/100.x address, never ws://<host>.local
Reuse the per-mode URL logic already in ConnectionTab (SettingsView.swift around line 779) rather than inventing a new scheme
xcodebuild build -project QuipMac/QuipMac.xcodeproj -scheme QuipMac -destination 'platform=macOS' succeeds

userStories.title: Mac 'Send to iPhone' share button
userStories.description: As a user away from my Mac, I want to share the pairing link from the Mac so I can AirDrop/Message/Mail it to the phone and tap to pair.
acceptanceCriteria: SecurityTab (QuipMac/Views/SettingsView.swift around line 1254) adds a 'Send to iPhone' button
The button builds the quip://pair link via PairingPayload(url: pairingURL(), pin: <current PIN>).encodedURL() plus a human-readable "<ws url>\nPIN: <pin>" text fallback
Tapping it presents NSSharingServicePicker over those items, reusing the existing diagnostics-share pattern (SettingsView.swift around line 1237) rather than a new mechanism
xcodebuild build -project QuipMac/QuipMac.xcodeproj -scheme QuipMac -destination 'platform=macOS' succeeds

userStories.title: Clarify the pairing screen (native Camera cannot open the QR)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the pairing screen to tell me the native Camera cannot scan it, so I use the in-app scanner or the share link instead of getting 'No usable data found'.
acceptanceCriteria: The QR header copy in SecurityTab no longer implies the native Camera works (e.g. 'Scan with iPhone' becomes 'Scan in the Quip app - the Camera app cannot open it')
The 'Send to iPhone' share button (US-004) is surfaced as the easy/remote alternative near the QR
No functional regression to the QR rendering itself
xcodebuild build -project QuipMac/QuipMac.xcodeproj -scheme QuipMac -destination 'platform=macOS' succeeds
